title: Mark Bible Quiz - Chapter 4
description: Ten questions on Mark 4: the parable of the sower and its explanation, the lamp on a stand, the growing seed, the mustard seed and the storm on the sea.

questions.text: Where did he sit while the whole multitude was on the land?
questions.explanation: A great multitude was gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat in the sea and sat down, while all the multitude were on the land by the sea.

answers.text: In a boat on the sea
At the door of a house

questions.text: What happened to the seed that fell by the road?
questions.explanation: As the farmer sowed, some seed fell by the road, and the birds came and devoured it.

answers.text: It yielded a hundred times as much
The birds came and devoured it

questions.text: Why did the seed on the rocky ground wither away?
questions.explanation: When the sun had risen it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered away.

answers.text: The ground was full of thorns

questions.text: How much did the seed that fell into the good ground produce?
questions.explanation: It yielded fruit, growing up and increasing: some produced thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times as much.

answers.text: Thirty, sixty or one hundred times as much
Two, five or ten times as much
Ten, twenty or forty times as much
Five, ten or fifteen times as much

questions.text: What does the farmer sow in the explanation of the parable?
questions.explanation: He said, "The farmer sows the word."

questions.text: Who takes away the word that was sown by the road?
questions.explanation: The ones by the road are those who, when they have heard, immediately have the word taken away from them by Satan.

questions.text: Where did he say a lamp is put?
questions.explanation: He asked whether the lamp is brought to be put under a basket or under a bed, and said that it is put on a stand.

questions.text: What did he compare God's Kingdom to in the parable of the smallest seed?
questions.explanation: He said it is like a grain of mustard seed, which is less than all the seeds on the earth, yet grows up and becomes greater than all the herbs.

answers.text: A fruit tree by the water

questions.text: Where was he when the big wind storm arose and the boat was filling?
questions.explanation: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion, and they woke him up.

answers.text: At the front of the boat, rowing
In the stern, asleep on the cushion
In a small boat beside them

questions.text: What did he say to the sea when he was woken up?
questions.explanation: He rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Peace! Be still!" The wind ceased and there was a great calm.

answers.text: "Let's go over to the other side."
